desc:
A fleet of buses runs independently. Bus i needs times[i] minutes for one trip and starts its next trip the moment the previous one ends, with no breaks. All buses start at minute 0.

Return the smallest number of minutes after which the buses together have completed at least totalTrips trips.

Example: times = [1, 2, 3], totalTrips = 5. After 3 minutes the buses have done 3 + 1 + 1 = 5 trips; after 2 minutes only 2 + 1 + 0 = 3. The answer is 3.
hints: After t minutes, how many trips has bus i finished?
It has finished t // times[i] trips. Adding this over all buses gives a total that never decreases as t grows.
Binary search t between 1 and min(times) * totalTrips (the fastest bus alone would do everything by then) and find the smallest t whose total is at least totalTrips.
editorial: The trip count by minute t is f(t) = sum(t // times[i]). It is non-decreasing in t, so the smallest t with f(t) ≥ totalTrips can be found by binary search. The fastest bus alone completes totalTrips trips in min(times) * totalTrips minutes, which is a valid upper bound (at most 109, so it fits in a 32-bit integer).

Each probe is O(n), and the range has size up to 10<sup>9</sup>, so the cost is about 30 probes of O(n). Time is O(n log(min(times) * totalTrips)), space O(1). You cannot simply simulate minute by minute, because the answer may be a billion minutes.
